description: ATS-optimized resume section guidelines for deterministic resume generation. Used by AI agents to populate resume fields given a job description, candidate data, and keyword sources.

Personal_information.description: Contact details and identity fields. Must appear at the top of the resume text block before any other section.

Contact_preferred_job_title.format: Target job title matching the job description when available

Contact_city.format: City, Region (do not include full street address)

Contact_portfolio_url.format: Full URL to portfolio or personal website

rules: Must appear at the top of the resume text block, before any other section.
No graphics or icons around personal information.
Do not include full street address; city and region are sufficient.
Use plain text only — no hyperlinks that rely on styling.
keyword_rules: Do not insert job description keywords into the personal information section.
formatting_constraints: Plain text, no tables or columns.
Name may be slightly larger font but must remain parseable text.
prioritization_logic: Always include Contact_full_name.
Include Contact_email and Contact_phone when available.
Include Contact_city when relevant to job location requirements.
Include Contact_preferred_job_title when it matches the target role.
Include Contact_linkedin_url when available.
Include Contact_portfolio_url only when relevant to the role.

Professional_summary.description: A concise career snapshot tailored to the target role. Must be 2–4 sentences or bullet points.

Professional_summary_text.format: 2–4 sentences or bullet points describing the candidate's career snapshot
Professional_summary_text.example: Results-driven Senior Software Engineer with 8+ years of experience building scalable web applications. Expert in React, Node.js, and cloud architecture with a track record of reducing deployment times by 40%. Passionate about delivering high-quality, user-centric solutions in fast-paced environments.

rules: Must be 2–4 sentences or bullet points.
Must be tailored using job description phrases (job title, at least 3 core skills).
Must use action verbs and measurable value statements where possible.
First sentence: role + experience level.
Second sentence: top skills matching the job posting.
Third sentence: value or impact the candidate delivers.
keyword_rules: Extract keywords from the job description and include them naturally in the summary.
Place the most relevant job title early in the summary.
Include at least 3 core skills from the job description.
formatting_constraints: Plain paragraph or simple bullet points.
No headers, footers, or graphics within the summary.
prioritization_logic: Prioritize keywords from must-have requirements over nice-to-haves.
Lead with the candidate's strongest alignment to the target role.
If measurable results exist, include the most impactful one.

Skills.description: A structured list of competencies divided into hard skills and soft skills.

Hard_skills.format: Array of technology, tool, and methodology names from the job description

Soft_skills.format: Array of interpersonal and contextual skill names; do not overemphasize

rules: Format as a bullet list or comma-separated list of competencies.
Divide into Hard_skills (technologies, tools, methodologies) and Soft_skills (contextual, not overemphasized).
Minimum 5 highest-priority skills matching the job posting.
Include synonyms and acronyms where applicable (e.g., 'ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning)').
Every listed skill must appear in the job description or be evidenced in the candidate profile.
Do not fabricate skills the candidate does not possess.
keyword_rules: Every listed skill must appear in the job description or candidate profile.
Use exact terminology from the job description when possible.
Include both the acronym and expanded form for common abbreviations.
Map skill keywords from the job description directly into this section.
formatting_constraints: Single-column layout, no multi-column or table formatting.
No icons or graphics next to skill names.
Group hard skills before soft skills.
prioritization_logic: List skills in order of relevance to the job description.
Must-have skills from the job description appear first.
Nice-to-have skills follow.
Candidate-only skills (not in JD) appear last, if space permits.

Work_experience.description: Professional experience entries in reverse chronological order with action-oriented bullet points.

Experience_entries.format: Array of experience objects in reverse chronological order

Experience_bullets.format: Array of achievement/responsibility strings beginning with action verbs
example: Led migration of monolithic architecture to microservices, reducing deployment time by 40%
Developed real-time data pipeline processing 2M+ events daily using Kafka and Python
Mentored team of 5 junior engineers, improving code review turnaround by 30%

rules: List experience in reverse chronological order (most recent first).
Each entry must include: company name, job title, start date, end date, and bullet points.
4–6 bullets for the most recent role; 2–4 for older roles.
Bullets must begin with action verbs (e.g., Led, Developed, Implemented, Managed).
Include measurable results where possible (percentages, dollar amounts, team sizes, etc.).
Follow the Action → Result → Skill bullet pattern.
Do not fabricate achievements or metrics not supported by candidate data.
keyword_rules: Include at least one keyword from the job description per bullet when applicable.
Analyze the job description and map required responsibilities to candidate bullets using equivalent vocabulary.
Use job-description terminology for tools, technologies, and methodologies mentioned in bullets.
Role titles should mirror JD language where truthful.
formatting_constraints: No tables, columns, or graphical elements.
Each bullet is a single paragraph.
prioritization_logic: Most recent and relevant roles appear first.
Roles directly matching the target position get more bullets.
Older or less relevant roles may be condensed or omitted if space is limited.
Bullets covering must-have requirements appear before nice-to-have coverage.

Education.description: Academic qualifications in reverse chronological order.

Education_entries.format: Array of education objects in reverse chronological order

rules: List in reverse chronological order.
Each entry must include institution name and degree at minimum.
Exclude GPA unless the industry standard expects it.
Include relevant certifications if formal degrees are missing.
Field of study is recommended but optional.
keyword_rules: Include degree names and fields of study that align with job description requirements.
If the job description mentions specific certifications, list them here if possessed.
prioritization_logic: Most recent and highest-level qualifications appear first.
Degrees relevant to the target role take priority.
Certifications relevant to the JD are included when formal degrees are absent.

Languages.description: Spoken languages with standardized proficiency levels.

Language_entries.format: Array of language objects with proficiency levels

Language_proficiency.format: One of: Native, Fluent, Intermediate, Basic

rules: Identify all spoken languages with proficiency levels.
Use standardized levels: Native, Fluent, Intermediate, Basic.
Only include languages relevant to the job if space is limited.
keyword_rules: If the job description specifies language requirements, ensure matching languages are listed.
Place job-required languages first in the list.
formatting_constraints: Format as 'Language — Proficiency' or a simple list.
prioritization_logic: Languages required by the job description appear first.
Native or fluent languages appear before intermediate or basic.
Omit languages at Basic level unless the JD specifically values them.

global_formatting_rules.bullet_points: Single paragraphs with simple dot bullets only.
global_formatting_rules.fonts: Assume default text output; avoid styling, bold, italic, or underline unless the rendering system supports it.
ats_compatibility: Use standard section headings exactly as specified.
Avoid creative or non-standard section titles.
Ensure all content is selectable, parseable plain text.
Do not embed information in graphics or images.

keyword_extraction_rules.description: Rules for extracting keywords from the job description and mapping them to resume sections.
extraction_steps: Identify job titles mentioned in the job description.
Identify hard skills: technologies, programming languages, frameworks, tools.
Identify soft skills: leadership, communication, collaboration terms.
Identify industry-specific terms and domain knowledge.
Identify key responsibilities and action phrases.
normalization_rules: Normalize synonyms to a canonical form (e.g., 'JS' and 'JavaScript' both map to 'JavaScript').
Expand acronyms on first use (e.g., 'CI/CD (Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment)').
Unify casing to title case for skill names.
Deduplicate keywords that refer to the same concept.

tailoring_rules.description: Rules for adapting the resume when candidate data does not fully match the job description.
rules: When candidate input does not include fields referenced in the job description, search for synonyms and semantically similar terms.
If the candidate does not possess a specified tool or skill, do not invent it — leave the field blank or omit it.
Use transferable skills and equivalent experience to bridge gaps where possible.
Flag missing must-have requirements as gaps for user review.
Prioritize truthful representation over keyword density.

validation_rules.description: Rules for verifying the final resume output.
rules: Every section must have at least one keyword match with the job description.
All date fields must be parsed in YYYY-MM format.
Resume text must be single-column and ATS-parsable.
No fabricated skills, experiences, or metrics.
All required fields must be populated (Contact_full_name at minimum).
Section order must match the defined section_order.
Bullet points must begin with action verbs.
Professional summary must contain at least 3 keywords from the job description.
